reason: Meiku keeps PIN quick unlock because it is substantially more reliable and usable for this single-vault product than the previous WebAuthn PRF implementation.
policy: security.md: authentication credentials and tokens must not be stored in localStorage
security_assessment: The persisted blob is AES-GCM encrypted with a key derived from a six-digit PIN (PBKDF2-SHA-256, one million iterations). Since v0.3.0 (DEC-003) it contains the vault data key and the server write secret, never the master password, so a brute-forced blob does not reveal a reusable password; a password change rotates the data key and invalidates every PIN. Plaintext write secrets are limited to sessionStorage, auto-lock remains five minutes, sign-out clears the PIN, legacy blobs are replaced after unlock and legacy passkey data is removed. Offline PIN guessing against a stolen browser profile remains the accepted residual risk and must be reviewed by the stated date.
